q1_issues.issue: Can is defined as a specific subject's capability on an event, or as a status operator wrapping a categorical Member/Inheritance atom, but here it wraps a GroupOf typing atom and is being used for impersonal possibility ('there can be'), so the modal is attached to the wrong content.
The uniqueness claim (CardinalityAtMost sk_victor_1 1) is asserted flat, outside the modal, so the parse states as fact what the sentence only says is possible.
sk_victor_1 has no top-level typing atom — its only class atom (GroupOf) sits inside the Can wrapper, leaving an untyped referent symbol at top level.

q2_gaps: impersonal / alethic possibility 'there can be …' — 'can' is licensed only as a specific subject's capability (Can e) or as deontic Permitted, with no operator for an existential possibility claim that has no subject whose ability it is

modal scope over an existential or a cardinality claim — status operators are specified for events and for copular Member/Inheritance atoms only, so there is no licensed shape for 'it is possible that at most one N exists'

exclusive 'but one / only one' on a singular existential — the Only focus particle needs a prejacent event plus a focused filler, and Cardinality/CardinalityAtMost are defined only over a group, so a singular 'one victor' has no stated encoding
notes: All three heads (Can, GroupOf, CardinalityAtMost) are licensed operators; the defect is the configuration — a status operator over GroupOf, with the modalized content asserted outside it. The archaic 'but' = 'only' was read correctly (not as the adversative connective), and CardinalityAtMost 1 is a defensible rendering of 'but one' once a group is minted.
